finding.evidence: `packages/backend/scripts/migrate-yorkie-cf-ranges.ts:214` `const client = new yorkie.Client({ rpcAddr, apiKey });` — no `authTokenInjector`. Same at `packages/backend/scripts/migrate-yorkie-worksheet-shape.ts:340` and `packages/backend/scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts:204,208`. All then `activate()` + `attach()` documents. verdict.reason: The absence is real and I could not find any counterexample. Enforcement is the default (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:95,109,133-135) and an absent token yields 401 UNAUTHENTICATED (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:55-59,200-205); only the service-token type short-circuits to ALLOW (:215-217). The delta's own fix in YorkieService injects that token (yorkie.service.ts:37,55-56,74), but the three standalone ops scripts construct `new yorkie.Client({ rpcAddr, apiKey })` with no `authTokenInjector` (migrate-yorkie-cf-ranges.ts:212-214, migrate-yorkie-worksheet-shape.ts:338-340, copy-yorkie-documents.ts:204-210) and then activate/attach. Repo-wide greps for `authTokenInjector|signYorkieServiceToken|yorkie-service-token` yield no hits under packages/backend/scripts, and greps for `process.env`/`JWT_SECRET` in those scripts show only YORKIE_RPC_ADDR/YORKIE_PUBLIC_KEY — so there is no indirect or env-supplied token path. The scripts are reachable via package.json:28-29 (`migrate:yorkie:cf-ranges`, `migrate:yorkie:worksheet-shape`) and direct tsx invocation. In lane for blast-radius (behaviour/config contract change with unupdated consumers outside the diff) and major: these sites now fail at attach on any deployment with the webhook methods registered.

finding.summary: Flipping the webhook default to ENFORCE denies the backend's own tokenless Yorkie client, breaking every server-side `withDocument` path
finding.evidence: `YorkieService.withDocument` attaches with `new yorkie.Client({ rpcAddr, apiKey })` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie.service.ts:42-55) — no `authTokenInjector`, no backend-minted Yorkie token (nothing in packages/backend/src mints one for itself; `signYorkieToken` is only exposed via `GET /auth/yorkie-token`). With the webhook methods registered as documented (`AttachDocument`, `PushPull`, `Watch`, … — packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:573-581), Yorkie calls `POST /internal/yorkie/auth` for those attaches with an empty token; `decide()` runs `verifyYorkieToken('')`, throws, and returns 401 UNAUTHENTICATED (packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:188-193). Before this change the stock deployment was in shadow mode and those calls were allowed anyway; now the stock deployment enforces, so all 103 `withDocument(...)` call sites — API v1 cells/worksheet/tabs/comments/docs-content/slides controllers, `document-copy.service.ts`, `template.service.ts`, `seed/seed-templates.ts` — fail on any deployment that registers the methods and configures nothing else. The fix belongs on the new default (exempt or authenticate the server-side client), not on each caller.

verdict.reason:
The finding's central factual claim — that `YorkieService.withDocument` attaches with a tokenless client and that nothing in `packages/backend/src` mints a Yorkie token for the backend itself — is false in this repository.

1. `packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie.service.ts:71-75` constructs the client as `new yorkie.Client({ rpcAddr, apiKey, authTokenInjector: this.authTokenInjector })`. The injector is set in the constructor (yorkie.service.ts:50-62) from `JWT_SECRET` and returns `signYorkieServiceToken(secret, expiresIn)`.

2. A backend service token minter exists: `packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-service-token.ts:27-46` (`YORKIE_SERVICE_TOKEN_TYPE = 'yorkie-service'`, `signYorkieServiceToken`), signed with the same `JWT_SECRET` that `AuthService` uses as its verification secret (`packages/backend/src/auth/auth.service.ts:58`).

3. The webhook accepts it: `verifyYorkieToken` explicitly permits `YORKIE_SERVICE_TOKEN_TYPE` (auth.service.ts:95-107, type union at auth.service.ts:41-44), and `YorkieAuthController.decide` short-circuits to ALLOW for that identity before any document-scoped checks (`packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:200-217`). So a server-side attach is authenticated and allowed under enforcement, not 401'd.

The claimed 401 path (`decide()` running `verifyYorkieToken('')`) is only reachable if `JWT_SECRET` is unset, which the code notes is impossible for a booted app since `AuthService.requireConfig('JWT_SECRET')` throws otherwise (auth.service.ts:58); that branch only logs a warning for bare tool/test constructions (yorkie.service.ts:57-62). No caller of `withDocument` is broken by the enforce default.
